newsitem.title: USA: Vermont jobless rate flat at 3.9 pct in March.
newsitem.headline: Vermont jobless rate flat at 3.9 pct in March.

text.p: Vermont's unemployment rate again was level at 3.9 percent in March, as hirings were soft in construction and government, Susan Auld, Commissioner of the state Department of Employment and Training said Tuesday.
The steady unemployment rate was, however, an improvment from the year-ago level, when it stood at 4.6 percent.
"Unemployment held steady for the third consecutive month. Jobs data, however, remained unimpressive due to weakness in construction and government activities," Auld said, in prepared remarks.

Paper producers and printing firms accounted for most of the weakness in nondurable manufacturing, which lost 200 jobs, when the data were not adjusted for seasonality. Significant drops also were seen at lodging and resort businesses, as winter recreation wound down.
The drops in the government sector mainly were due to shifting employment at state colleges, and accounted for most of the 400 jobs lost in this area.
The following list provides a detailed breakdown of Vermont's labor markets. The data were not seasonaly adjusted.
--Barre-Montpelier, 5.0 pct, down from 5.8 pct in Feb and 6.1 pct a year-ago.
--Bennington-Manchester, 4.5 pct, down from 4.9 pct and 5.1 pct a year-ago.
--Burlington, 3.0 pct, down from 3.3 pct in Feb and 3.5 pct a year-ago.
--Enosburg, 8.9 pct, down from 10.2 pct in Feb and 10.3 pct.
--Hartford-Lebanon, Vermont-New Hampshire, 2.1 pct, down from 2.3 pct in Feb and 2.6 pct a year-ago.
--Keene-Brattleboro, New Hampshire, Vermont portion only, 3.2 pct, down from 3.3 pct in Feb and 3.8 pct a year-ago.
---Middlebury, 4.9 pct, down from 5.6 pct in Feb and 5.8 pct a year-ago.
--Morristown-Stowe, 5.8 pct in March, down from 6.2 pct in Feb and 6.9 pct a year-ago.
--Newport, 9.5 pct, down from 10.2 pct in Feb and 10.0 pct a year-ago.
--Randolph, 4.0 pct, down from 4.6 pct in Feb and 4.8 pct a year-ago.
--Rutland, 4.4 pct, down from 5.0 pct in Feb and level with a year-ago.
--St Johnsbury, 5.9 pct, down from 6.7 pct in Feb and 6.5 pct a year-ago.
--Springfield, 4.3 pct, down from 4.4 pct in March and 5.0 pct a year-ago.
